title: [functorch] Specialize activation-checkpointing minimum cut
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #197724

Activation checkpointing builds large, sparse directed flow graphs with nonnegative capacities. NetworkX's general-purpose minimum-cut machinery constructs and traverses a dictionary-backed residual graph, making representation overhead a visible part of compilation.

Convert the graph to dense integer indices and flat adjacency and residual arrays, then solve it with an iterative Dinic algorithm. Detect a true all-infinite source-to-sink path before solving and route it directly through the existing unbounded-graph diagnostics. Large finite INT_INF penalties remain regular solver inputs.

Tests compare cut values and partitions against NetworkX, cover long non-recursive paths, and distinguish finite sentinel penalties from truly unbounded paths.

Benchmark:

Median cold compile-and-run time from two fresh-cache runs of each adjacent commit state, using the same worker settings:

```
Model 1: 68.765s -> 68.516s  (-0.249s, -0.36%)
Model 2: 63.984s -> 57.538s  (-6.446s, -10.07%)
Model 3: 66.681s -> 59.861s  (-6.820s, -10.23%)
Model 4: 51.819s -> 51.609s  (-0.211s, -0.41%)
Model 5: 64.720s -> 61.731s  (-2.989s, -4.62%)
Mean:    63.194s -> 59.851s  (-3.343s, -5.29%)
```
